Subject: Renewal questions — price hold and surge capacity

Hi Naomi,

Hope you’re well — our renewal for next quarter is approaching and we need to confirm two things before we lock dates with procurement: 1) whether Redwood can extend a price hold for 12 months on the rates in our current SOW if we commit to a 20% uplift in committed capacity, and 2) short-term surge capacity (up to +40%) for a 6-week marketing push in Q3.

Our procurement team wants to avoid a broader RFP if we can get a clean addendum with those guardrails. Can you share the commercial approach and any precedent for a temporary surge bucket with capped overage rates?

Thanks — Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Digital
renewals@acmedigital.com

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask. High level: we can offer a 12-month price hold tied to a 20% baseline commit uplift, plus a temporary surge bucket for the six-week window with a defined overage cap.

What I’ll do:
- Loop in Ben (pricing) for exact numbers and the draft addendum.
- Jordan (CS/ops) will confirm technical feasibility for the surge window and any lead time needed for provisioning.

1) Is the 20% uplift applied to monthly committed GPU-hours or to token volume/embedding units?
2) Do you expect the surge pattern to be a single contiguous 6-week period or several intermittent bursts totaling 6 weeks?

If you can reply with those, we’ll turn around a redline-ready addendum in 48 hours.

Hi Maya — attaching a proposed commercial addendum for review (see RDW_Acme_Renewal_Addendum_2027_v1.pdf) and a capacity worksheet (capacity-plan-acme-2027.xlsx). Key points:

- 12-month price hold: we will lock current per-GPU-hour pricing for 12 months from the effective renewal date contingent on a 20% uplift in committed GPU-hours (baseline monthly commit increases from 5,000 to 6,000 GPU-hours).
- Surge bucket: 40% temporary surge (2,400 GPU-hours) available during a single contiguous 6-week window. Surge usage billed at a fixed overage rate equal to 1.6x standard on-demand rate; overage is capped at 20% of the total monthly invoice for the surge period.
- Early termination / stepdown: if actual monthly consumption over the first 3 months is lower than 85% of the new commit, standard true-up applies, but price hold remains in effect for the 12-month term.
- Implementation: Jordan, ops needs two weeks lead time to carve the surge capacity and validate routing.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, confirm and we’ll issue a DocuSign addendum.
2) If procurement wants a different overage multiplier, flag that in a reply and we’ll run scenarios.

Attaching: RDW_Acme_Renewal_Addendum_2027_v1.pdf (draft addendum), capacity-plan-acme-2027.xlsx (provisioning worksheet).

Regards,
Ben Carter

- Narrow the surge-cap overage cap language to be explicit: cap applies as a hard invoice ceiling for the surge months (not prorated across other months).
- Add a clause that surge provisioning confirmation (ops readiness) is scheduled no later than 6/25/2027 to guarantee the July start.
- Can we soften the overage multiplier from 1.6x to 1.4x if Acme commits to a short-term prepayment equal to 25% of the estimated surge consumption?

Procurement would like to move quickly — if you can incorporate these three changes we’ll sign the addendum and push the renewal through next week.
